questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The structure of Maltose is a non-reducing sugar.
Statement II: The structure of Lactose is a reducing sugar.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explain:
Statement I is false: Maltose is a disaccharide consisting of two alpha-D-glucose units linked by an $\alpha(1 \to 4)$ glycosidic bond. The second glucose ring contains a free anomeric carbon (hemiacetal), enabling it to mutarotate and act as a reducing sugar.
Statement II is true: Lactose is a disaccharide containing beta-D-galactose and beta-D-glucose linked via a $\beta(1 \to 4)$ bond. It also maintains a free hemiacetal on the glucose unit, functioning as a reducing sugar.

questions.q:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I (Name of amino acid)
A. Arginine
B. Aspartic acid
C. Lysine
D. Glutamic acid
List-II (One letter symbol/type)
I. D/Non-essential
II. R/Essential
III. E/Non-essential
IV. K/Essential
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explain:
Amino acids have standard one-letter codes and biological classifications:
A. Arginine is an essential amino acid (in some contexts semi-essential for children but classically listed to ensure its critical availability), and its one-letter symbol is R. (A -> II)
B. Aspartic acid is a non-essential amino acid, synthesized within the body, symbolized by D. (B -> I)
C. Lysine is a strictly essential amino acid, not synthesized by the body, symbolized by K. (C -> IV)
D. Glutamic acid is a non-essential amino acid, and its one-letter code is E. (D -> III)
The correct sequence is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.
